objective.value: Design and demonstrate a novel DERA-based synthetic pathway in E. coli that converts formaldehyde (HCHO) and ethanol into 1,3-propanediol (PDO) via three metabolic modules: an ACALD supply module (ethanol to acetaldehyde), a HCHO supply module, and a DERA-based PDO production module (aldol condensation of HCHO and ACALD to 3-HPA, then reduction to PDO).
objective.notes: Objective stated in Abstract, Results and Discussion (pathway design) and Conclusion.

hypothesis.value: Acetaldehyde (ACALD), not pyruvate, is the real HCHO acceptor in C-C bond formation; the authors hypothesized that an aldolase (DERA) can catalyze the aldol condensation of HCHO and ACALD to form 3-hydroxypropionaldehyde (3-HPA), which can then be reduced to PDO, yielding a theoretically 100% carbon-conserving, vitamin B12-independent PDO pathway.
hypothesis.notes: Stated as an explicit research question in Results and Discussion; theoretical carbon utilization is an author claim, not a measured value.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Authors actively designed and implemented a new three-module metabolic pathway using ACALD as the HCHO acceptor; passes Q1 (pathway construction), Q2 (implemented in this study), Q3 (genuine design choice).
ddr_annotations.design_action: Use acetaldehyde as the aldol acceptor for HCHO via DERA to form 3-HPA, then reduce 3-HPA to PDO via DhaT, assembled as a three-module pathway (ACALD supply, HCHO supply, DERA-based PDO production) in E. coli BL21(DE3).
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Pathway design stated in results_and_discussion_p001/p003 and access_p014; implemented and verified in EXP1/EXP2.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Prior observation (from the authors' previous KHB-based work) that the carboxyl group of pyruvate is not involved in the aldol condensation and is removed in the next step, indicating acetaldehyde is the real HCHO receptor (results_and_discussion_p001). Precedes the design action.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type: experimental_measurement (in vivo PDO formation with 13C verification, Figure 4, Table 1) supporting feasibility; the design premise itself derives from reaction-mechanism analysis of the prior pathway.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: The choice of ACALD as acceptor is derived from analysis of the KHB reaction mechanism (pyruvate carboxyl not participating), stated before pathway construction.

generalizable_rule.statement: Acetaldehyde can serve as an aldol acceptor for formaldehyde via DERA to form 3-hydroxypropionaldehyde, enabling a theoretically carbon-loss-free route to 1,3-propanediol when combined with a 3-HPA reductase such as DhaT.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: E. coli BL21(DE3) resting-cell bioconversion coexpressing DERA (DERA_ECO or DERA_TMA) and DhaT with HCHO+ACALD (10-100 mM) or HCHO+ethanol; in vitro with purified enzymes at 30 °C, pH 7.0.
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: Other hosts, other aldehyde acceptors, other aldolases not tested, growth-coupled fermentation, industrially relevant titers, thermodynamic driving-force limitations (authors note all three reactions are reversible).
generalizable_rule.evidence_basis: mechanistic_inference plus experimental demonstration (Table 1, Figures 4 and 6)

ddr_annotations.alternatives_considered: Pyruvate-based KHB pathway (prior work, ref 16) has carbon loss via decarboxylation; chemical aldol condensation of HCHO and ACALD requires >250 °C with side reactions (dehydration, oligomerization, polymerization) and was rejected in favor of biocatalysis (results_and_discussion_p002).

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Selection of DERA_TMA after a screening campaign; passes Q1 (enzyme choice implemented as expression constructs), Q2 (screen performed in this study), Q3 (active selection among candidates).
ddr_annotations.design_action: Screen four DERAs from heat-resistant bacteria (plus DERA_ECO) coexpressed with DhaT in E. coli BL21(DE3) and select DERA_TMA from Thermotoga maritima for the PDO production module.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: results_and_discussion_p006: 'we tested four kinds of DERAs from heat-resistant bacteria since it was suggested that heat resistance is related to aldehyde tolerance'; DERA_TMA gave highest PDO (8.20 ± 0.04 mM, Table 2).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: DERA_ECO catalyzed the condensation (1.02 mM PDO preliminary trial) but a more efficient DERA was sought; literature suggested heat resistance relates to aldehyde tolerance (ref 34). Precedes the selection.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type: screening_result / experimental_measurement (Table 2 in vivo comparison; Figure 5 in vitro activity and tolerance data).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Final choice based on measured in vivo PDO titers and in vitro specific activity/HCHO tolerance; the initial candidate pool was motivated by a literature suggestion (heat resistance ~ aldehyde tolerance).
ddr_annotations.alternatives_considered: DERA_ECO, DERA_GTH, DERA_SEP, DERA_PAE tested in vivo (Table 2); DERA_Rd3BB tested in vitro; KHG-type aldolases and Yfau/PanB screened earlier (Table 1) with low or no PDO.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Choice of DhaT from K. pneumoniae DSM 2026 as the 3-HPA reductase; passes Q1/Q2/Q3 but with sparse in-paper rationale.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Coexpress NADH-dependent PDO oxidoreductase DhaT from Klebsiella pneumoniae DSM 2026 to reduce 3-HPA to PDO.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: DhaT used in all coexpression constructs (results_and_discussion_p004, citing ref 32; materials_and_methods_p002).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: The designed pathway requires reduction of 3-HPA to PDO (pathway design, access_p014). Precedes enzyme choice.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type: literature_precedent (ref 32) for the choice; experimental_measurement in this study shows DhaT supports at least ten times DERA_TMA activity without 3-HPA accumulation (results_and_discussion_p006).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: No explicit comparison of reductases is reported; DhaT was adopted from prior literature (dha regulon, ref 32). In-paper rationale is minimal, so no bounded rule candidate is emitted despite the allowed reason nature.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Design and implementation of the ACALD supply module; passes Q1 (HpADH1 expression construct), Q2 (this study), Q3 (explicit design choice with stated rationale).
ddr_annotations.design_action: Generate ACALD in situ from ethanol by expressing alcohol dehydrogenase HpADH1 from Hansenula polymorpha, instead of direct ACALD addition.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: a_in_vivo_dera_assay_p011: direct ACALD addition 'would be too expensive or inconvenient for the operation and harmful for the biocatalyst' and NADH balance is critical; HpADH1 chosen as showing good performance on ethanol to acetaldehyde (refs 39, 40).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Recognized cost/operational/toxicity problems of direct ACALD addition and the need for NADH balance, stated before module construction (a_in_vivo_dera_assay_p011).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type: literature_precedent (refs 39,40) for enzyme choice; experimental_measurement in this study (in vitro module verification Figure S1C,D - supplement unavailable; in vivo improvement 5.67 to 10.91 mM, Figure 6B,C; 13C-ethanol verification Figure 6A).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: HpADH1 selected based on reported performance in literature; the in situ ACALD-from-ethanol concept additionally rests on practical and cofactor-balance reasoning stated by the authors.

generalizable_rule.statement: Expressing HpADH1 to oxidize ethanol can supply acetaldehyde in situ for DERA-based PDO synthesis in E. coli whole-cell bioconversion, avoiding direct acetaldehyde feeding and roughly doubling PDO titer under the tested conditions.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: E. coli BL21(DE3) resting cells (OD600 = 50) coexpressing DERA_TMA, HpADH1 and DhaT; 300 mM ethanol + 100 mM HCHO; 30 °C, 230 rpm, limited oxygen, batch mode.
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: Other ADHs (not tested), other hosts, growing-cell fermentation, other alcohol substrates, aerobic/anaerobic regimes other than the tested limited-oxygen setup.

ddr_annotations.alternatives_considered: Direct ACALD addition (rejected: expensive, inconvenient, harmful to the biocatalyst); other ADHs mentioned as a large pool but not individually compared.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Deletion of the competing endogenous HCHO-consuming pathway; passes Q1 (genome editing), Q2 (performed in this study), Q3 (flux-redirection design choice).
ddr_annotations.design_action: Delete the frmA gene (encoding HCHO dehydrogenase of the frmRAB system) in E. coli BL21(DE3) using CRISPR-Cas9, yielding strain BF16.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: The relatively low PDO yield from ethanol and HCHO is partly caused by conversion of HCHO to formate, as previously reported in the authors' earlier study (a_in_vivo_dera_assay_p012). Stated before the knockout.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type: experimental_measurement (BF16 vs BF12: 12.75 ± 0.44 mM, 0.128 mol/mol vs 10.91 ± 0.08 mM, 0.11 mol/mol; reduced HCHO consumption, Figure 6D).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Rationale is a stated metabolic mechanism (frmA encodes HCHO dehydrogenase converting HCHO to formate; removing it redirects HCHO toward PDO) established before the edit.

generalizable_rule.statement: Deleting frmA reduces endogenous formaldehyde consumption to formate and increases PDO titer and yield in DERA-based whole-cell bioconversion in E. coli BL21(DE3).
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: Resting-cell batch bioconversion of BF12 vs BF16 with 100 mM HCHO + 300 mM ethanol at 30 °C, OD600 = 50.
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: Other hosts, other HCHO-assimilation pathways, complete elimination of formate formation (formate was still produced in fed-batch despite ΔfrmA), growth-coupled conditions.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Construction and testing of DERA point mutants for aldehyde tolerance; passes Q1 (site-directed mutagenesis), Q2 (constructed in this study), Q3 (design choice guided by literature mechanism). Outcome did not lead to adoption in the final strain.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Construct and purify DERA_ECO C47M, DERA_ECO C47V and DERA_TMA C65M mutants and test their tolerance toward HCHO.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Literature: ACALD forms a covalent bond with C47 of DERA_ECO causing irreversible deactivation, and C47M alleviates inactivation (Dick et al. 2016); a C47V mutant from S. halifaxensis retains activity at >400 mM ACALD (Huffman et al. 2019). Cited before mutant testing.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type: literature_precedent for the mutation choice; experimental_measurement for outcomes (residual activities after 0.3 M HCHO pretreatment: C47V 85%, C47M 99%, Rd3BB 94% vs DERA_TMA 61%, DERA_ECO wt 50%; DERA_TMA C65M lost 70% activity).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Mutation sites directly adopted from published mechanism studies. Results were mixed (pretreatment tolerance improved but activity still suppressed by reaction HCHO; TMA C65M largely inactive), so no positive rule candidate is emitted.
ddr_annotations.alternatives_considered: Wild-type DERA_ECO and DERA_TMA; DERA_Rd3BB (naturally tolerant variant) tested in parallel.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Process-level design choice to control HCHO concentration; passes Q1 (fed-batch intervention), Q2 (this study), Q3 (deliberate strategy based on prior measurement).
ddr_annotations.design_action: Perform fed-batch whole-cell bioconversion with ten interim HCHO additions to keep HCHO concentration above approximately 0.6 mM, eliminating diol byproducts.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: a_in_vivo_dera_assay_p019 ('the HCHO concentration was thus kept over 0.6 mM to eliminate the formation of diol byproducts') and a_in_vivo_dera_assay_p020 (fed-batch implementation, Figure 8).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Diol byproducts were found to be generated only when HCHO was nearly completely consumed, and in vitro assays showed HCHO above 0.6 mM strongly inhibits ACALD self-condensation and its condensation with 3-HPA (a_in_vivo_dera_assay_p019, Figure 7F). Measured before the fed-batch design.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type: experimental_measurement (in vitro HCHO-dependence assay Figure 7F; fed-batch outcome: no diol byproducts, PDO 17.35 ± 0.58 mM, 0.096 mol/mol at 24 h).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: The feeding strategy is directly derived from the measured inhibitory effect of HCHO on the byproduct-forming DERA side reactions; mechanism (competing condensations) characterized in this study before the process change.

generalizable_rule.statement: Maintaining formaldehyde above approximately 0.6 mM suppresses DERA_TMA-catalyzed formation of 1,3-BDO, C5 and C6 diol byproducts and increases PDO titer in whole-cell bioconversion with intermittent HCHO feeding.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: BF16 resting cells (OD600 = 50), initial 100 mM HCHO + 300 mM ethanol, ten interim HCHO additions, 30 °C, 230 rpm, limited oxygen, 24-30 h.
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: Continuous feeding strategies, other hosts or enzymes, high-HCHO regimes that suppress the aldol condensation itself (activity drops at high reaction HCHO), methanol/formate side fluxes (methanol reached 56.47 mM at 30 h).

ddr_annotations.alternatives_considered: Methanol-based in situ HCHO supply via Mdh2 (EXP7) was attempted as an alternative HCHO supply module but gave only 1.05 mM PDO due to Mdh bottleneck.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Implementation of a methanol-based HCHO supply module; passes Q1 (Mdh2 expression), Q2 (this study), Q3 (design choice), although it underperformed.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Express methanol dehydrogenase Mdh2 (EC 1.1.1.244) from B. methanolicus MGA3 in strain BF17 to oxidize methanol to HCHO as an in situ HCHO supply module.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: a_in_vivo_dera_assay_p018: 'To develop a HCHO supply module, methanol was first used as substrate. We selected a methanol dehydrogenase (Mdh2...)'.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: The stated goal of developing a HCHO supply module (modular pathway design, results_and_discussion_p003). No specific prior observation motivating Mdh2 over alternatives is reported.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type: experimental_measurement (whole-cell bioconversion gave only 1.05 mM PDO after 42 h; in vitro verification identified Mdh activity as bottleneck, Figure S1E - supplement unavailable).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: The paper states the selection of Mdh2 but reports no reason for choosing this specific enzyme; rationale therefore coded as not reported.
